questions.question: After building with output: "standalone", which folders must you copy into the container yourself if the container serves them?
questions.explanation: The standalone output contains traced files and a minimal server.js, but not public/ or .next/static, because those are meant to be served from a CDN.

questions.question: Users intermittently see "Failed to find Server Action" when requests land on different pods. What is the fix?
options: Use sticky sessions and a longer terminationGracePeriodSeconds
Provide the same NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY at build time so every instance shares one encryption key
questions.explanation: Server Action closures are encrypted with a per-build key. Building with a shared NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (ideally one image promoted everywhere) keeps all pods compatible.

questions.question: Why is baking a staging API URL into a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable a problem when you promote one image from staging to production?
options: NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are encrypted and cannot be read in production
NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are inlined at build time, so the staging value ships to production in the bundle
NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are only read in development
Docker strips all environment variables starting with NEXT_
questions.explanation: Public variables are replaced in the bundle during next build. Keep per-environment values server-side and read them at request time instead.

questions.question: With deploymentId set, what happens when a browser on version v41 navigates and the request reaches a pod running v42?
options: The v42 pod serves v41 chunks from its cache
The request fails with a 500 error
The server detects the mismatch and the router performs a hard navigation (full reload) to load a consistent set of assets
The load balancer retries until it finds a v41 pod
questions.explanation: The x-deployment-id header lets the server spot version skew; a full reload avoids missing chunks or unknown Server Action IDs, at the cost of losing client state.
